design_rationale:
[1] WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. The customer asks for one thing: pay the fee that keeps her flight credit alive. The record shows the credit (credit_holdings.5cda5415-115d-4fad-a6d9-6fa0cceb6cdf, Crestline Flight Credit CX2046183951) already expired on 2026-08-31 with 412.60 written off, so an extension is no longer possible ('an expired credit is handled by reinstatement instead', base credit_extension) and the fee she means is a reinstatement fee. The fee rule states outright that the fee waits on a record-visible state: 'The reinstatement fee is fixed only after the credit carries the restore entry that brings back the value written off at its expiry.' The agent must read that, see there is no restore entry, work out from the reinstated-validity rule that the reinstatement write is the one that books it, compute a nine-month reinstated term from five factors, reinstate, and only then compute a six-factor fee on the world that now carries the 412.60 restore. Difficulty comes from reading policy, querying six tables and doing the arithmetic, not from tool guessing: there is exactly one reinstatement tool and one fee tool.
[2] SCOPE SNAPSHOT (task 0 of 2). Already occupied: nothing. Claimed by task 0: credit_ext_reinstated_validity (target reinstate_credit_8e2d0d7d, agent) and credit_ext_reinstatement_fee (target pay_credit_reinstatement_fee_177d2025, owner=user). Reserved headroom for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisite problems, factor counts [5,5,5]): the telephone redemption fee (credit_service_fee, phone_redemption_fee), the extension fee (credit_service_fee, extension_fee) and the extension itself (credit_extend) remain unclaimed and chain naturally on an active credit near its expiry, so task 1 has an independent three-problem tree with its own customer-owned fee payment.
[3] DRAW (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[6, 5]. The root credit_ext_reinstatement_fee takes 6 factors; the prerequisite credit_ext_reinstated_validity takes 5.
[4] PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: credit_ext_reinstatement_fee (customer's own card payment, owner=user). Edge root -> credit_ext_reinstated_validity: kind value_input, gate rf_restored_value, form state, prerequisite sentence (in the root's own rule) 'The reinstatement fee is fixed only after the credit carries the restore entry that brings back the value written off at its expiry.' Four-point test: (1) ordering connective 'only after', joining the policy's own result (the fee) to what it waits on, affirmative direction - the way a fee desk states a charge that rests on something being in place; rewritten negated it reads 'the reinstatement fee is not fixed until the credit carries the restore entry ...', same condition; (2) the waited-on side is a record state (a restore entry on the credit's ledger), no action or performer named; (3) no tool, policy id or snake_case token; (4) strength 'only after' is a hard requirement, scope 'the restore entry that brings back the value written off at its expiry' names exactly the credit_reinstatement_restore kind. State form is legal because exactly one write of this difficulty books a restore entry: reinstate_credit_8e2d0d7d (the other tools book only service-fee entries or update the expiry). Derivation: sentence + records (credit_ledger has a write-off e5a300dd-1c20-4dba-96e2-a6477eedf4af and no restore) + the reinstated-validity rule ('Reinstating an expired credit gives it a new term of validity ...') and the base rule 'Reinstatement restores exactly the value written off at expiry in one restore entry' -> the one action is reinstating the credit, resolved_by reinstate_credit_8e2d0d7d (agent). Unresolved at frozen_time: credit_holdings.5cda5415-115d-4fad-a6d9-6fa0cceb6cdf.status = expired, remaining_value 0.0, write-off 412.60 on 2026-09-01, no restore entry. Topological order: reinstated validity (step 10) then fee (step 12). Deletion sensitivity (replay with step 10 skipped): fee_amount 58.95 -> 0.00 (basis tier falls to 30 percent of 0.00), and the terminal credit stays expired. No parallel edges. user_scenario never says 'expired', 'reinstate', 'restore' or 'write-off'; the tools validate no prerequisite (pay_credit_reinstatement_fee_177d2025 books the entry for any amount on any credit).
[5] BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Step 10 subject credit_reinstate: governing base policy credit_reinstatement; gate reinstatement_window (time): 'A reinstatement must be requested no later than reinstatement_window_days_after_expiry calendar days after the credit's expiry date as recorded on the credit.' Anchor credit_holdings.expiry_date 2026-08-31, duration variants.reinstatement_window_days_after_expiry = 90 (Flight Credit), counted in calendar days from the day after the expiry date, last day inclusive -> last accepted day 2026-11-29; frozen 2026-09-15 is day 15, satisfied; 2026-11-30 would fail. Prose conditions also hold: reinstatement_permitted true, reinstatement_count 0 < max_reinstatements 1. Step 12 subject credit_service_fee: governing base policies credit_redemption_rules (no gate on fees -> policy_scope), credit_extension (gate fee_on_live_credit: 'A credit fee entry is charged only on a credit whose status is active or expired.' - status active after step 10) and credit_reinstatement (no gate on fees -> policy_scope; its fee waiver is inherited: Summit Gold has credit_service_fees_waived false, so the fee is charged).
[6] OVERWRITES (declared, clause level). credit_ext_reinstated_validity supersedes credit_reinstatement 'sets the new expiry_date to the reinstatement date plus reinstated_validity_months calendar months with the same month-end fallback as issuance' (evaluated on this world base gives 6 months / 2027-03-15, the extended rule gives 9 / 2027-06-15). credit_ext_reinstatement_fee supersedes credit_reinstatement 'The reinstatement_fee is charged as a separate fee entry before the credit is reinstated' (base: flat 150 charged first; extended: 58.95 charged once reinstated, because the fee basis now rests on the value restored). Every other base clause (window, count limit, restore of exactly the written-off value, waiver, fee on a live credit) is inherited unchanged; base params values are untouched.
[7] FACTOR CARD - credit_ext_reinstated_validity (5 factors, 4 parameter + 1 method; result 9, all-baseline 6). member_standing_term (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty; its tier and qualifying-dollar conditions come from the one membership record, so it is not counted as multi-source): upper tier (any Summit Platinum, Diamond or Chairman member, or a Summit Gold member at the Gold threshold) - Summit Gold, 9860.00 >= 9000 -> 8 (baseline 6 -> result 7). written_off_value_months (parameter, history): write-off 412.60 in [250,500) -> +1 (baseline 0 -> 8). membership_tenure_months (parameter, cross loyalty date): enrolled 2016-02-11, 127 whole months >= 120 -> +2 (baseline 0 -> 7). prior_use_months (parameter, history): 1 redemption, fewer than many_redemptions 2 -> +1 (baseline 0 -> 8); the 25.00 telephone fee entry of 2026-02-03 beside it is a service-fee entry, not a redemption. reinstatement_lateness (method, date): 15 days from the recorded expiry date 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-15, in [15,30] -> sum x 3/4 rounded down (baseline 'as they stand' -> 12). Near-miss: a careless reader counting from the write-off date 2026-09-01 (the day the credit closed) gets 14 days, the 'used as they stand' tier, and 12 months; the rule anchors the count on 'the credit's expiry date as recorded on the credit'.
[8] FACTOR CARD - credit_ext_reinstatement_fee (6 factors, 5 parameter + 1 method; result 58.95, all-baseline 150.00). reinstatement_fee_basis (method, history, the value_input gate): value restored 412.60 in [250,600) -> lesser of 150 and 35 percent (144.41) (baseline flat 150 -> 61.24). reinstatement_fee_member_rate (parameter, cross-difficulty loyalty, multi-source Summit tier AND count of flight accruals in 12 months): Gold with 6 -> 0.70 (baseline 1 -> 84.22); rows outside the count: loyalty_activity.4c9016c0-d1c6-46af-a8d8-6c897225f156 (flight accrual 2025-09-10, 12 whole months back, outside the window) and loyalty_activity.cbfa9e24-529d-49ca-a101-897b4f3bfcf0 (co-branded card partner accrual, not a flight accrual), and the seven loyalty_mqd_accrual rows the flights trigger - none of them counts. This is the task's genuine multi-source factor: the tier comes from loyalty_holdings, the count from loyalty_activity. reinstatement_fee_source_fare_rate (parameter, cross ticket): source ticket 45d4581c-be73-4d41-bd40-4ecba9f40fc5 Crestline Premium Economy -> 0.80 (baseline 1 -> 73.69). reinstatement_fee_history_rate (parameter, history): net fees 25.00 -> 0.90 (baseline 1 -> 65.50). reinstatement_fee_disruption_rate (parameter, cross ticket history): one controllable record 82b83a20-d0f2-4ffc-b745-89cc7b2dccb0 -> exactly one -> 0.90 (baseline 1 -> 65.50); near-misses defdc211-311a-47b7-b308-6b7171f1085c (2026-02-14 delay) and 2f9e1531-088a-4876-a183-33f0773f53fe (2026-06-12 cancellation of CR1407) are classified uncontrollable and are excluded by the rule's 'controllable cause' - counting either lands on the many_disruptions tier (0.75) and gives 49.13 instead of 58.95. reinstatement_fee_cardmember_rate (parameter, cross companion): companion_holdings.01e2720c-8729-45b0-9d2e-86bfefc731ea active Main Cabin certificate from the co-branded card anniversary, no pass -> 0.90 (baseline 1 -> 65.50). No stamp names any outcome; every tier rests on ledger rows, dates or another product's records.
[9] BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target object: credit_holdings.5cda5415-115d-4fad-a6d9-6fa0cceb6cdf (credit_number CX2046183951), the customer's only credit. Rows aggregated: its credit_ledger rows only (load 19d7f40b-0e5c-47e3-b38c-859beb8aff0b, redemption 61c7dcb5-2b8f-42c7-a39c-bbe56269d1cf, telephone fee f175a9a1-c86b-4dca-8a90-bdba5a4eddcd linked by related_entry_id to that redemption, write-off e5a300dd-1c20-4dba-96e2-a6477eedf4af). The restore points at the write-off by reversed_entry_id; the fee entry carries the credit_id. Cross-product rows read: loyalty_holdings.979809f8-df80-494b-ae1c-64c305bd4e87, fifteen loyalty_activity rows (7 flight accruals, their 7 triggered mqd accruals, 1 card partner accrual), four tickets (source ticket 45d4581c-be73-4d41-bd40-4ecba9f40fc5, redeemed ticket 8a4cc2c7-6b26-488c-a5dd-c58b0e917132, 2026-06 ticket eff91880-0030-4ddc-bcf5-4139ddcc18b7, April 2026 First ticket bc03a957-4dfe-4eb1-91c2-8e4a5a8dd299), three disruption records, one companion certificate.
[10] WORLD ROWS AND WHY. customers: identity. credit_holdings/credit_ledger: the expired credit and its history (write-off = restored value and written-off-value months; redemption = prior-use months; telephone fee = fee-history rate). loyalty_holdings: tier, qualifying dollars, enrolment (standing term, tenure, waiver). loyalty_activity: seven flight accruals (six in the rolling 12-month window), each with its triggered loyalty_mqd_accrual; the 2026 qualifying-dollar rows (86.05 + 86.04 + 4723.26 + 4723.25 + 241.40) sum to the membership's 9860.00; plus one co-branded card partner accrual. ticket_holdings also carries the April 2026 CLT-LHR Crestline First round trip that earned most of those qualifying dollars. ticket_holdings: source fare brand (Premium Economy), and the tickets the disruptions sit on. ticket_disruptions: one controllable and two uncontrollable records. companion_holdings: the co-branded card certificate. Removing any of these changes a factor tier and the scored number (see sensitivity figures). Automatic-clause check: the credit is expired and stays so until step 10; no other credit exists, the companion certificate is active and unused (no obligation), tickets are closed; nothing else falls due. No stale cache is used (remaining_value 0.00 equals the ledger).
[11] PERSONA. Gwendolyn Farrow, brisk marketing director calling between meetings; volunteers only the goal (keep the credit alive, pay the fee today) and the true context (cancelled Seattle trip last fall, credit good for about a year); gives mobile number, date of birth, email, ZIP, credit number, Summit number and the co-branded card only when asked; reacts passively: dismayed if told it ran out and asks what that means for the money on it, agrees if told something must be done on the credit first, pays exactly the amount the agent quotes when handed the payment, and ends once told the fee is paid and the credit is usable. She knows no amounts and never proposes a figure; she raises no other request. Her last reaction answers the last gold action (the payment).
[12] REACHABILITY WALK. Turn 1: she asks to keep the credit alive and pay the fee. Agent asks for details -> 7045552318 locates, date of birth 1983-04-17 verifies (2 matches). Credit lookup shows it expired 2026-08-31 -> agent explains; she asks what that means for the money on it. The KB fee rule's prerequisite sentence and the validity rule lead to reinstatement; she says go ahead. Agent reads ledger, Summit account and activity, tickets, disruptions, companion products; computes 9 months; reinstates (receipt: restore entry, expiry 2027-06-15). Agent computes 58.95 and hands over the payment; she runs it and reads back the fee entry number if asked. All at 2026-09-15 11:20 CT; nothing waits on a real-world event (reinstatement and card payment are synchronous desk actions).
[13] EASY MISTAKES. Treating the request as an extension (the credit is past its expiry date); charging the flat 150 (baseline); computing the fee before reinstating (basis 0.00); counting lateness from the write-off date (14 days) or ignoring the lateness adjustment (12 months); counting the uncontrollable delay or cancellation, or the partner accrual; forgetting the fee is not waived for Gold.
[14] STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION. Reads: find_customers, verify_customer_identity, find_credit_holdings, find_credit_ledger, find_loyalty_holdings, find_loyalty_activity, find_ticket_holdings, find_ticket_disruptions, find_companion_holdings. Writes in topological order: reinstate_credit_8e2d0d7d(credit_id, writeoff_entry_id=e5a300dd-1c20-4dba-96e2-a6477eedf4af, restored_value=412.60, validity_months=9) then the customer's pay_credit_reinstatement_fee_177d2025(credit_id, fee_amount=58.95). Verification ran the policy compute through skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py machinery on the handling-time world (replay of gold writes): validity 9 on the opening world; fee 58.95 on the world after step 10; per-factor baselines validity 7/8/7/8/12 and fee 61.24/84.22/73.69/65.50/65.50/65.50; all-baseline 6 and 150.00; skipping step 10 gives fee 0.00. Gate outputs (after revision c): check_compute --task 0 COMPUTE OK; replay_tasks REPLAY OK (13 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, closure 20/20); check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cross_fire SCOPE OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK.
[15] RULE <-> COMPUTE SWEEP. Forward: every world-reading or choosing binding quotes its ladder sentence verbatim in compute_basis (rt_* and rf_* entries). Reverse: validity rule sentences on order (sum, then lateness, then cap), each ladder, the lateness count 'from the credit's expiry date as recorded on the credit' -> DAYS(F('expiry_date'), NOW), and 'whole calendar months' -> MONTHS are all claimed; fee rule sentences on the waiver (rf_fee_waived), the order 'rates multiplied with one another into one combined rate ... only that product is rounded to the nearest cent' (rf_combined_rate, RND on the result only), and each ladder are claimed. No binding carries a window or filter the rule does not state (12-month windows, controllable cause, flight accruals only, net of fee refunds all stated).
[16] SOLVABILITY AND BLIND DRAFT. solvability_contract: step 10 reinstatement_window evidence credit_id/expiry_date/reinstatement_count + frozen_time; step 12 fee_on_live_credit evidence credit_id/status + prior_step 10; policy_scope for credit_redemption_rules and credit_reinstatement on the fee. Blind draft from visible context only (published rules, tool schemas, finder returns, persona lines): the only credit is expired -> the fee rule waits on a restore entry -> the reinstatement is the write that books one -> term 8+1+2+1=12, 15 days late -> 9 -> reinstate -> restored 412.60 -> basis 144.41 -> rates 0.70, 0.80, 0.90, 0.90, 0.90 -> 58.95. Same object, same order, same values as gold.
[17] REVISIONS. (a) Seed: flight accruals first carried qualifying dollars; corrected to 0.00 because qualifying dollars post as separate mqd entries in the loyalty charter (the membership's qualifying_dollars_ytd is the authoritative running figure). (b) Near-misses sharpened: the 2026-06-12 cancellation reclassified as uncontrollable (so the disruption count is 1 and a careless count of either uncontrollable record gives the 0.75 tier and 49.13), and many_redemptions set to 2 (so counting the same-day telephone fee entry as a redemption would give the +2 tier); fee recomputed from 49.13 to 58.95 and propagated to computations, tracing, closure and this dossier; validity unchanged at 9. Gates re-run green. (c) The validity computation had no near-miss that moved its number (a +1 miss is absorbed by the three-quarter rounding), so frozen_time moved from 2026-09-24 to 2026-09-15: lateness from the recorded expiry date is now exactly 15 days (three-quarter tier) while a count from the write-off date gives 14 (as-they-stand tier, 12 months); the out-of-window flight accrual moved to 2025-09-10 to stay 12 whole months back. Validity stays 9 (new expiry 2027-06-15) and the fee stays 58.95; all references updated and gates re-run. (d) Symptom: the fee rule's opening sentence said the fee is charged 'once the credit has been reinstated', a second, action-form wording of the dependency the prerequisite sentence already states. Change: the opening sentence now reads 'The reinstatement fee is charged as a separate fee entry on the credit, and it is waived when ...', and the overwrite's replaced_by quotes the prerequisite sentence itself (the sentence that retires base's 'before the credit is reinstated'). Propagated to compute_basis and tracing; check_extended and check_solvability re-run OK. ROUND 2 (policy-task audit rework; items from audits/policy_task/flight_credits_and_vouchers/_difficulty.md and 0.md). G-1/T0-F1 (RED): symptom - the member-standing ladder's fall-through gave Summit Platinum, Diamond and Chairman holders the standard 6 months while a Gold holder at the Gold threshold got 8. Root cause - the fall-through 'every other holder' swept the tiers above Gold. Change: the ladder is now upper_standing_term_months (8) for any Summit Platinum, Diamond or Chairman member and for a Summit Gold member at the Gold threshold; middle_standing_term_months (7) for any other Summit Gold member and for a Summit Silver member at the Silver threshold; the standard term for everyone else. No tier ever gets less than a tier below it. This customer (Gold, 9860.00 >= 9000) stays on the upper tier: validity 9, sensitivity 7, all-baseline 6 are unchanged (check_compute re-run). G-2: the cardmember rate now decides by existence - EXISTS an active Companion Pass Semiannual or Annual, else EXISTS an active co-branded card anniversary certificate - so a customer holding several companion products is rated exactly as the rule says; this world's rate stays 0.90. G-4/T0-O2: the rule now defines its windows ('A reinstatement-fee window of the last so many calendar months holds the entries dated fewer than that many whole calendar months before the date the reinstatement fee is worked out, so it rolls back from that date and is not a count of completed calendar months.'), which is the reading compute uses. G-8/T0-O4: every seeded flight accrual now carries its triggered loyalty_mqd_accrual row, and the April 2026 First round trip CLT-LHR (two coupons, 4723.26 and 4723.25 eligible fare) was added so the 2026 mqd rows sum exactly to qualifying_dollars_ytd 9860.00; mile_balance moved to 161570 to reflect it. The flight-accrual count in the window becomes 6 (same 0.70 tier), and no scored figure moves (fee 58.95, all six sensitivities unchanged). T0-O1: her reaction to hearing the credit ran out is now 'you ask what that means for the money on it', a question about the outcome that does not steer toward reviving the credit. T0-O3: the multi-source labels are corrected above (member_standing_term is a same-record conjunction; the task's multi-source factor is reinstatement_fee_member_rate). G-3 does not touch this task (it has no telephone fee problem); G-5, G-6 and G-7 are accepted as observations with no change. Gates re-run green after each change.
user_scenario:
You are Gwendolyn Farrow, a marketing director in Charlotte who flies Crestline a few times a year and is calling between two meetings, so you are friendly but brisk and like plain answers. Last fall you cancelled a round trip to Seattle and Crestline turned the ticket into a flight credit. You know a credit like that is only good for about a year, and you have heard that Crestline lets you pay a fee to keep a credit alive. You open the call by saying you want to keep the credit alive and would like to pay that fee today so you do not lose the money. You have not checked the credit's dates lately and do not know whether anything has happened to it; you have no trip booked and are not asking to book one.

You give your details only when the agent asks for them, one or two at a time: your mobile number is 7045552318, your date of birth is 1983-04-17, your email is gwen.farrow@lakemail.com and your billing ZIP code is 28207. If the agent asks which credit, it is the one from the cancelled Seattle trip, and if they want the number you read it off the old confirmation email: CX2046183951. If they ask for your Summit number, it is 2084417356. If they ask whether you hold the Crestline co-branded card or any companion certificate, you say yes, you have the card and a companion certificate came with it this spring, but you have not used it. You do not remember any amounts on the credit and tell the agent to go by what their system shows.

If the agent tells you the credit has already run out, you are a little dismayed that you let it slip, and you ask what that means for the money on it. If the agent explains that something has to be done on the credit to bring it back before anything else, you tell them to go ahead and do it. When the agent tells you what the fee comes to and hands you the payment step, you pay it yourself by card for exactly the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the receipt or entry number the payment shows if the agent asks for it. You do not argue about the size of the fee, and you do not suggest any figure of your own. If the agent asks whether you want anything else changed on the credit, you say no, keeping it usable is all you wanted. Once the agent confirms the fee is paid and the credit is usable again, you thank them and end the call.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Gives the written-off value (written-off-value months, restored_value), the write-off entry id the restore points at, the redemption count (prior-use months) and the net service fees (reinstatement-fee fee-history rate); shows no restore entry exists.

evaluation_criteria.necessity: Decides the member-standing term (Gold with qualifying dollars at the Gold threshold), the membership-tenure months (127 whole months) and that the reinstatement fee is not waived.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the Summit activity to count flight accruals posted in the last 12 calendar months.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The reinstatement-fee member rate needs the count of loyalty_flight_accrual entries in the rolling 12-month window (6), excluding the 2025-09-10 accrual and the co-branded card partner accrual.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's tickets, including the Premium Economy ticket the credit arose from.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The reinstatement-fee source-fare rate reads the fare brand of the source ticket (Crestline Premium Economy).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the irregular-operations records on the customer's tickets.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The reinstatement-fee disruption rate counts controllable-cause disruption records in the last 12 months (1), excluding the uncontrollable delay of 2026-02-14 and the uncontrollable cancellation of 2026-06-12.
The reinstatement-fee cardmember rate needs to know she holds no companion pass but an active co-branded card anniversary companion certificate.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the reinstatement tool named by the reinstated-validity policy.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Reinstate the expired credit: status active, expiry 2027-06-15, reinstatement count 1, and book back the 412.60 written off in one restore entry that points at the write-off entry.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: credit_ext_reinstated_validity computes validity_months = 9; its restore entry is the state the reinstatement-fee rule waits on, so this write must land before the fee is worked out.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_id: 5cda5415-115d-4fad-a6d9-6fa0cceb6cdf. Basis: the credit lookup returns the Crestline Flight Credit with credit_number CX2046183951 whose source ticket is the cancelled CLT-SEA Premium Economy ticket, the one the customer describes as 'the one from the cancelled Seattle trip'. Uniqueness: she holds exactly one credit, so any agent converges on this reference.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.writeoff_entry_id: e5a300dd-1c20-4dba-96e2-a6477eedf4af. Basis: the reinstatement rule says 'Reinstatement restores exactly the value written off at expiry in one restore entry', and the event credit_reinstatement_restore carries reversed_entry_id 'expiry write-off restored'; the value history shows exactly one credit_expiry_writeoff entry on the credit (2026-09-01, 412.60). Uniqueness: no other write-off exists on the credit.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.restored_value: 412.60. Basis: 'Reinstatement restores exactly the value written off at expiry in one restore entry' (credit_reinstatement rule, not superseded); the only write-off entry is 412.60. Uniqueness: the amount is read, not chosen; any other figure would restore a different value than was written off.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.validity_months: 9. member-standing term 8 (Summit Gold, qualifying dollars 9860.00 >= Gold threshold 9000) + written-off-value months 1 (412.60 is >= 250 and < 500) + membership-tenure months 2 (enrolled 2016-02-11, 127 whole months >= 120) + prior-use months 1 (one redemption entry, fewer than many_redemptions 2; the telephone fee entry is not a redemption) = 12; lateness 15 calendar days from the recorded expiry date 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-15 is >= 15 and <= 30 (counting from the write-off date would give 14 and the wrong tier), so 12 x 3/4 rounded down = 9; cap max_term_months 12 does not bite. The tool sets the new expiry to 2026-09-15 plus 9 months = 2027-06-15.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the customer's reinstatement-fee payment tool so it can be handed to her.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair for the customer's own payment; no DB effect.

evaluation_criteria.objective: The customer pays the reinstatement fee of 58.95 by card; one reinstatement_fee service-fee entry is booked on the credit.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: credit_ext_reinstatement_fee computes fee_amount = 58.95 on the world after the reinstatement; the payment is the customer's own card payment, so the agent hands it over and she runs it.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_id: 5cda5415-115d-4fad-a6d9-6fa0cceb6cdf. Basis: the same credit the agent just reinstated; the fee rule says 'The reinstatement fee is charged as a separate fee entry on the credit' and 'The reinstatement fee is fixed only after the credit carries the restore entry that brings back the value written off at its expiry.' Uniqueness: only one credit was reinstated; the agent gives this reference to the customer when handing over the payment.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.fee_amount: 58.95. Basis 144.41: after the restore the value restored is 412.60 (>= 250 and < 600), so the basis is the lesser of reinstatement_fee 150 and 35 percent of 412.60 = 144.41. Combined rate 0.40824 = member rate 0.70 (Summit Gold with 6 flight accruals dated fewer than 12 whole calendar months back, at least 4) x source-fare rate 0.80 (source ticket Crestline Premium Economy) x fee-history rate 0.90 (net service fees 25.00, above zero and below 50) x disruption rate 0.90 (1 controllable disruption record in 12 months; the two uncontrollable ones do not count) x cardmember rate 0.90 (active co-branded card anniversary certificate, no pass). 144.41 x 0.40824 = 58.9539..., rounded to the cent = 58.95; not waived because Summit Gold has credit_service_fees_waived false.

factor_trace: member_standing_term (parameter): loyalty_holdings.979809f8-df80-494b-ae1c-64c305bd4e87 shows Summit Gold with qualifying_dollars_ytd 9860.00 against the Summit Gold qualifying_dollars_threshold 9000 in the loyalty charter, so the upper tier applies (a Summit Gold member whose qualifying dollars have reached the Gold threshold; Platinum, Diamond and Chairman members sit on the same tier) and selects upper_standing_term_months = 8; the baseline (the instrument's reinstated_validity_months) is 6 and would give a result of 7.

written_off_value_months (parameter): SUM of credit_expiry_writeoff on the credit = 412.60 (credit_ledger.e5a300dd-1c20-4dba-96e2-a6477eedf4af), at least mid_writeoff_usd 250 and below high_writeoff_usd 500, so mid_writeoff_extra_months = 1; the baseline adds none and would give 8.

membership_tenure_months (parameter): Summit enrolled_date 2016-02-11 to 2026-09-15 is 127 whole calendar months, at least long_tenure_months 120, so long_tenure_extra_months = 2; the baseline adds none and would give 7.

prior_use_months (parameter): COUNT of credit_redemption on the credit = 1 (credit_ledger.61c7dcb5-2b8f-42c7-a39c-bbe56269d1cf), at least one and fewer than many_redemptions 2, so some_redemption_extra_months = 1 (the 25.00 telephone fee entry of the same day is a service-fee entry, not a redemption); the baseline adds none and would give 8.

reinstatement_lateness (method): expiry_date 2026-08-31 to 2026-09-15 is 15 calendar days, at least three_quarter_from_days 15 and no more than halving_after_days 30, so the summed 12 months are multiplied by three quarters and rounded down = 9 (near-miss: counting from the write-off date 2026-09-01 gives 14 days, the 'used as they stand' tier, and 12); the baseline uses the sum as it stands and would give 12.
result: MN(max_term_months 12, 9) = 9 whole calendar months, so the new expiry date is 2026-09-15 plus 9 months = 2027-06-15.

the value written off at expiry is at least mid_writeoff_usd and below high_writeoff_usd
the Summit membership was enrolled at least long_tenure_months whole calendar months before the reinstatement date
the credit carries at least one and fewer than many_redemptions redemption entries
at least three_quarter_from_days and no more than halving_after_days calendar days have passed

factor_trace: reinstatement_fee_basis (method): after the reinstatement at step 10 the credit carries one credit_reinstatement_restore entry of 412.60, at least small_restore_usd 250 and below mid_restore_usd 600, so the basis is the lesser of reinstatement_fee 150 and 35 percent of 412.60 (144.41) = 144.41; the baseline (the flat reinstatement_fee 150) would give 61.24.

reinstatement_fee_member_rate (parameter): Summit Gold, and loyalty_activity shows 6 loyalty_flight_accrual entries dated fewer than 12 whole calendar months before 2026-09-15 (2025-11-21, 2026-02-14, 2026-02-18, 2026-04-08, 2026-04-19, 2026-06-12; the loyalty_mqd_accrual rows each flight triggers are not flight accruals; the 2025-09-10 accrual is 12 whole months back and the 2026-09-06 entry is a partner accrual), at least active_flight_accruals 4, so gold_flyer_rate 0.70; the baseline rate 1 would give 84.22.

reinstatement_fee_source_fare_rate (parameter): the source ticket 45d4581c-be73-4d41-bd40-4ecba9f40fc5 was sold as Crestline Premium Economy, so premium_brand_rate 0.80; the baseline rate 1 would give 73.69.

reinstatement_fee_history_rate (parameter): service fees on the credit 25.00 (the telephone fee of 2026-02-03) less refunds 0.00 = 25.00, above zero and below fees_high_usd 50, so fees_some_rate 0.90; the baseline rate 1 would give 65.50.

reinstatement_fee_disruption_rate (parameter): controllable disruption records on the customer's tickets in the last 12 months = 1 (the 2026-02-18 delay on CR2064); near-misses: the 2026-02-14 delay and the 2026-06-12 cancellation of CR1407 are both classified uncontrollable, and counting either would reach many_disruptions 2 and rate 0.75; so one_disruption_rate 0.90; the baseline rate 1 would give 65.50.

reinstatement_fee_cardmember_rate (parameter): no active companion pass, and an active Crestline Companion Certificate Main Cabin issued as cobrand_card_anniversary, so cobrand_certificate_rate 0.90; the baseline rate 1 would give 65.50.
rf_fee_waived (plumbing): Summit Gold has credit_service_fees_waived false, so the fee is charged.
result: 144.41 x 0.40824 = 58.9539..., rounded to the nearest cent = 58.95.

edges.condition: The credit's ledger carries a credit_reinstatement_restore entry for the amount of its credit_expiry_writeoff entry, and the credit's status is active.
edges.policy_source: The reinstatement fee is fixed only after the credit carries the restore entry that brings back the value written off at its expiry.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: At 2026-09-15 the credit is still expired: its expiry write-off of 412.60 stands and no restore entry exists on its ledger, so the value restored is 0.00.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The reinstatement at step 10 books a credit_reinstatement_restore entry of 412.60 pointing at the write-off entry and sets the credit active with expiry 2027-06-15; rf_restored_value becomes 412.60 (verified by replay).

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single edge, so there is no parallel pair to reorder. The order is pinned by the prerequisite sentence of the fee rule ('The reinstatement fee is fixed only after the credit carries the restore entry that brings back the value written off at its expiry.'): the fee basis reads the value restored, so a fee paid ahead of the reinstatement is computed on 0.00 and lands as a different fee entry (0.00 instead of 58.95), a different terminal hash.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Replay with step 10 skipped: rf_restored_value stays 0.00, the basis tier falls to 30 percent of 0.00, and the scored fee_amount goes from 58.95 to 0.00; the terminal credit also stays expired with no restore entry and expiry 2026-08-31 instead of active, 412.60 remaining and expiry 2027-06-15.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario never says the credit has expired, never uses the words reinstate or reinstatement, and never mentions a restore, a write-off or a term of validity. The customer only asks to keep the credit alive and pay the fee; she learns it has run out only if the agent tells her, and her agreement to 'go ahead and do it' is a passive reaction to the agent's own explanation.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: task_tools.py: pay_credit_reinstatement_fee_177d2025 reads the credit row only for its customer_id and then unconditionally creates the credit_service_fee entry for the amount given; it never looks at the credit's status, restore entries or expiry, never refuses and never returns an error. reinstate_credit_8e2d0d7d likewise updates the credit and books the restore entry for whatever it is given.
